title: Relative categorical cylinders detect equivalence of diagrams
statement:
Use small simplicial sets, quasicategories, internal functor simplicial sets and inverse-and-two-triangle equivalence edges as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and categorical equivalences as in [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure]. Let $A\subseteq B$ be a degreewise simplicial subset. Write $B\amalg_A B$ for the simplicial set obtained by gluing two copies of $B$ along their copies of $A$, degree by degree. A categorical mapping cylinder for $B$ relative to $A$ means a small simplicial set $\overline B$, maps $s_0,s_1:B\to\overline B$, and a categorical equivalence $\pi:\overline B\to B$ such that $\pi s_0=\pi s_1=\operatorname{id}_B$, $s_0|_A=s_1|_A$, and the induced map $B\amalg_A B\to\overline B$ is degreewise injective.
Let $Q$ be a quasicategory, let $f_0,f_1:B\to Q$ have the same restriction $f_A:A\to Q$, and let $(\overline B,s_0,s_1,\pi)$ be any such categorical mapping cylinder. Define $\operatorname{Fun}_{f_A}(B,Q)$ to be the simplicial set whose $r$-simplices are maps $H:B\times\Delta^r\to Q$ with $H|_{A\times\Delta^r}=f_A\circ\operatorname{pr}_A$. Then there is an equivalence edge from $f_0$ to $f_1$ in $\operatorname{Fun}_{f_A}(B,Q)$ if and only if there exists a simplicial map $\overline f:\overline B\to Q$ with $\overline f s_0=f_0$ and $\overline f s_1=f_1$. The assertion includes $A=\varnothing$, when the relative functor simplicial set is $\operatorname{Fun}(B,Q)$.

source.place: Corollary 4.6.3.11, with Definition 4.6.3.3 (01K5) for categorical mapping cylinders. Kerodon tags, not Stacks tags. Read online 2026-10-17; not archived under literature/.

proof.text: Put $D=\operatorname{Fun}_{f_A}(B,Q)$. By [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-exponentiation], restriction $\operatorname{Fun}(B,Q)\to\operatorname{Fun}(A,Q)$ is an isofibration between quasicategories, hence an inner fibration. Its degreewise fiber at the vertex $f_A$ is exactly $D$: a simplex in the fiber is a map $B\times\Delta^r\to Q$ restricting to the constant $r$-simplex at $f_A$. This fiber is a quasicategory. Indeed, a horn in the fiber gives an inner-horn lifting square for restriction with bottom map the constant simplex at $f_A$; a filler is again in the fiber. Let $J=N(\mathcal J)$ be the two-object indiscrete groupoid nerve in [lem-coef-quasicategory-invertible-interval]. For any simplicial map $J\to T$, the images of the edges $01$ and $10$ and of the $2$-simplices $010$ and $101$ give an edge, its inverse, and both inverse triangles in $T$: the long edges of those two triangles are the degenerate edges $00$ and $11$. Thus such a map gives an equivalence edge with exactly the convention of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones].

source.place: Proposition 4.1.4.6 (01GQ), as cited in Theorem 4.6.3.8 (01KA); relative fiber identification and inverse triangles are written explicitly. Restriction isofibration: Corollary 4.4.5.3 (01F3).

proof.text: First assume that $F:\overline B\to Q$ extends both $f_0$ and $f_1$. In the Joyal model structure of [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure], factor $\pi$ as $\overline B\xrightarrow{j}E\xrightarrow{p}B$, with $j$ a trivial cofibration and $p$ a fibration. Since $\pi$ and $j$ are weak equivalences, two-out-of-three makes $p$ a weak equivalence, hence a trivial fibration. The weak factorization systems in that node therefore give: $p$ lifts against every monomorphism, while $j$ lifts against every fibration. The map $Q\to *$ is a fibration because $Q$ is a quasicategory. The square with top $F$, left $j$, and right $Q\to *$ has a filler $F':E\to Q$ with $F'j=F$. Set $t_\varepsilon=js_\varepsilon$; then $pt_\varepsilon=\operatorname{id}_B$, the restrictions of $t_0,t_1$ to $A$ agree, and $F't_\varepsilon=f_\varepsilon$. These operations take place in the input universe by the factorization assertion of the cited model-structure node. No quasicategory hypothesis on $B$, $\overline B$ or $E$ is used.

source.place: Theorem 4.6.3.8 (01KA), proof of (2) implies (3): replace the categorical equivalence by a trivial-cofibration/fibration factorization; two-out-of-three and terminal fibrancy give the stated lifts.

proof.text: Consider the simplicial subset $P=(B\times\{0,1\})\cup(A\times J)$ of $B\times J$, where $\{0,1\}\subset J$ consists of the two constant vertices and their degeneracies. Define $a:P\to E$ to be $t_0,t_1$ on the two copies of $B$, and to be $t_0|_A\circ\operatorname{pr}_A$ on $A\times J$. These formulas agree on the intersections $A\times\{0,1\}$ because $t_0|_A=t_1|_A$, so they define a simplicial map degree by degree. Moreover $pa=\operatorname{pr}_B|_P$. The inclusion $P\hookrightarrow B\times J$ is degreewise injective, so the trivial fibration $p$ constructed in step 2 has a lift $L:B\times J\to E$ with $L|_P=a$ and $pL=\operatorname{pr}_B$, by the weak factorization system of [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure]. The composite $F'L$ restricts to $f_0,f_1$ at $0,1$ and to $f_A\circ\operatorname{pr}_A$ on $A\times J$. Currying therefore gives a map $J\to D$ with endpoints $f_0,f_1$. Its edges and $2$-simplices $01,10,010,101$ supply the inverse-and-two-triangle equivalence as in step 1. This proves the extension-to-equivalence implication, and in fact produces a $J$-map in the strict relative fiber.

source.place: Theorem 4.6.3.8 (01KA), trivial-fibration lifting argument; here applied directly to the explicit relative J-prism to exhibit the equivalence edge, instead of appealing to a homotopy-class quotient.

proof.text: Conversely, suppose there is an equivalence edge $\eta:f_0\to f_1$ in $D$. The section $s_0$ is degreewise injective, since $\pi s_0=\operatorname{id}_B$. Since $\pi$ is a weak equivalence, two-out-of-three in [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure] makes $s_0$ a weak equivalence; it is thus a trivial cofibration. Lift $f_0$ against the fibration $Q\to *$ to obtain $G:\overline B\to Q$ with $Gs_0=f_0$. Put $g_1=Gs_1$; it restricts to $f_A$ on $A$. Apply the already proved steps 2-3 to $G$ and its endpoints $f_0,g_1$ to get a $J$-map between those vertices of $D$. Its two inverse triangles give an isomorphism $a:f_0\cong g_1$ in $hD$, the category presented by vertices, edges and $2$-simplex composition relations in [lem-coef-quasicategory-invertible-interval]. Likewise the two inverse triangles of $\eta$ give an isomorphism $b:f_0\cong f_1$ in $hD$. The ordinary composite $b\circ a^{-1}$ is an isomorphism from $g_1$ to $f_1$. Since $D$ is a quasicategory by step 1, [lem-coef-quasicategory-invertible-interval] now gives a map $v:J\to D$ with endpoints $g_1,f_1$. In uncurried form it is $V:B\times J\to Q$ with $V|_{B\times\{0\}}=g_1$, $V|_{B\times\{1\}}=f_1$ and $V|_{A\times J}=f_A\circ\operatorname{pr}_A$. This use of steps 2-3 is one-way: those steps were proved without assuming the present converse.

source.place: Corollary 4.6.3.11 (01KD), converse direction proved by first extending one endpoint and correcting the other by a strict relative equivalence; invertible interval: Cisinski Theorem 1.6.6 and Section 3.5.

proof.text: Let $C=B\amalg_A B$ and write $k:C\hookrightarrow\overline B$ for the monomorphism given in the statement. On $C\times J$, define $T$ to be $f_0\circ\operatorname{pr}_B$ on the first copy $B\times J$ and to be $V$ from step 4 on the second. The two formulas agree on $A\times J$, so define a simplicial map on the degreewise pushout; degreewise product with $J_r$ carries this pushout to the corresponding pushout of sets. Currying gives a simplicial map $J\to\operatorname{Fun}(C,Q)$ whose initial vertex is $Gk$ and whose final vertex is the glued diagram $u=(f_0,f_1):C\to Q$. The images of $01,10,010,101$ again show that its edge from $Gk$ to $u$ is an equivalence, without any pointwise-equivalence criterion or relative quotient identification. By [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-exponentiation], restriction $k^*:\operatorname{Fun}(\overline B,Q)\to\operatorname{Fun}(C,Q)$ is an isofibration. Lift this equivalence edge with specified source $G$ using the equivalence-lifting clause of that node. Its final vertex is a map $\overline f:\overline B\to Q$ with $\overline f k=u$ exactly, hence $\overline f s_0=f_0$ and $\overline f s_1=f_1$. This proves the converse for the prescribed cylinder. If $A=\varnothing$, the fiber condition in step 1 is empty and $D=\operatorname{Fun}(B,Q)$, giving the stated special case.

source.place: Corollary 4.6.3.11 (01KD) and Theorem 4.6.3.8 (01KA), the endpoint correction made explicit using Corollary 4.4.5.3 (01F3).

proof_origin.place: Theorem 4.6.3.8, Corollary 4.6.3.11 (01KD). Agent-written variant using existing Joyal weak factorization systems and restriction isofibrations: explicit relative J-prism for necessity and equivalence lifting for sufficiency. Online sources read 2026-10-17; not archived.

split_report.summary: Proved the cylinder criterion without new nodes. The relative functor fiber is a quasicategory by restriction isofibration. A Joyal trivial-fibration replacement lifts an explicit relative J-prism, giving the necessity and its strict inverse triangles. For sufficiency extend one endpoint, compare its other endpoint inside the strict relative fiber, glue a J-map on the endpoint pushout and lift the resulting equivalence through restriction. Statement unchanged. No use of the criterion itself or a model homotopy-class identification.
